uses.description:
Switches the typeface used to draw all text that follows this point in the string. The change persists for the remainder of the text block, so later text keeps the new font until another font change occurs. The tag itself renders nothing, contributing no visible characters of its own.

If the supplied name is not one of the game's built-in fonts, the text silently reverts to the block's starting font instead of reporting an error.

optional.name: Argument 1
optional.description: The name of the font to switch to, which must be one of the game's built-in fonts. If omitted, or if the name is not a recognised font, the text falls back to the font the block started with rather than failing.

uses.description:
Replaces the tag with a line of procedurally generated non-language speech for the actor the text is being shown for, of the kind used to represent creatures and characters who do not speak in words. The generated babble is built from the actor's personality — more intelligent actors produce longer, more varied output with more punctuation — and is between two and four sentences long, capped by the number of caret-separated segments in the surrounding text. If no actor is associated with the text, nothing is produced.

The generated line is then trimmed from the front, two characters at a time, until it fits within the available line width, so the visible result is the tail end of the babble rather than the whole of it. This tag also switches the font for the remainder of the text.

The whole behaviour is skipped, producing nothing at all, when the text block begins with an opening parenthesis — the convention for a parenthetical or narration line rather than spoken dialogue.

optional.name: Argument 1
optional.description: The font used to draw the generated speech and all text after it, which must be one of the game's built-in fonts. If omitted, or if the name is not a recognised font, the text falls back to the font the block started with.

uses.description:
Starts a new line: drawing moves down by one line height and back to the left edge of the text area, and the font is reset to the block's starting font. The tag itself renders no visible characters.

The whole behaviour is skipped when the text block begins with an opening parenthesis — the convention for a parenthetical or narration line rather than spoken dialogue — so in that case the tag has no effect at all.

Changes how fast the text that follows is typed out during the character-by-character reveal used in dialog. The multiplier applies to every piece of text after the tag and stays in effect until another speed change or the end of the text block, so it can be used to rush through filler or slow down a dramatic line. The tag itself renders no visible characters.

This only affects the reveal animation; text that is displayed all at once is unaffected. The multiplier stacks on top of the game's global dialog speed setting, so a player who has sped up dialog still sees a proportionally faster version of the requested pacing.

optional.name: Argument 1
optional.description: The speed multiplier: 1 is the normal typing rate, values above 1 reveal text faster and values below 1 reveal it more slowly. If omitted or left empty, the speed resets to normal. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

uses.description:
Inserts a timed pause into the character-by-character reveal of dialog text at the point where the tag appears. When the reveal reaches this spot it stops for the requested duration before continuing with the rest of the line, which is the usual way to write a beat, a hesitation, or a dramatic silence into a piece of dialog. The tag itself renders no visible characters and takes up no space.

The pause is queued rather than applied immediately, so it fires only when the reveal animation actually reaches that position. If the player skips ahead and reveals the whole block at once, the queued pause is consumed with everything else and no delay is felt.

optional.name: Argument 1
optional.description: How long to pause, in the same units as the text reveal timer — larger numbers hold longer. If omitted or left empty, a default pause of 0.7 is used. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

uses.description:
Draws a line of text centred within the remaining width of the text area and then starts a new line, which is the usual way to write a heading above a body of text. Centring is measured against the space left between the current drawing position and the right edge, so a title placed at the start of a line is centred across the full width, while one placed after existing text is centred only within what remains.

The supplied text is rendered in whatever font and colour are currently in effect. Because the argument is a plain value, it cannot itself contain an equals sign.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The text to draw as the centred heading. It is measured in the current font to work out the centring offset and is then drawn as-is, followed by a line break, so it must not contain an equals sign.

uses.description:
Draws a line of text pushed inward from the current position and then starts a new line, producing an indented heading or sub-heading. The text is shifted right by a quarter of the gap between the current drawing position and the right edge of the text area, so it sits noticeably in from the margin without being centred.

The supplied text is rendered in whatever font and colour are currently in effect. Because the argument is a plain value, it cannot itself contain an equals sign.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The text to draw on the indented line. It is measured in the current font to work out the indent offset and is then drawn as-is, followed by a line break, so it must not contain an equals sign.

uses.description:
Draws an image from the game's art at double size, on its own line and centred horizontally within the text area. Drawing first moves down one line, then the image is placed so that its doubled width is centred, and the drawing position afterwards sits at the image's bottom-right corner, so following text continues below and to the right of it rather than beside it.

Nothing is drawn if the name given is empty or the single character 0 — a deliberate no-op that is useful when the name is supplied indirectly through a global variable or formula. If the name is not one of the game's images the tag draws nothing and the game logs an error.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. Supplying an empty value or the single character 0 draws nothing instead of failing.

uses.description:
Draws an image from the game's art at triple size, on its own line and centred horizontally within the text area. Drawing first moves down one line, then the image is placed so that its tripled width is centred, and the drawing position afterwards sits at the image's bottom-right corner, so following text continues below and to the right of it rather than beside it.

Nothing is drawn if the name given is empty or the single character 0 — a deliberate no-op that is useful when the name is supplied indirectly through a global variable or formula. If the name is not one of the game's images the tag draws nothing and the game logs an error.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. Supplying an empty value or the single character 0 draws nothing instead of failing.

uses.description:
Draws an image from the game's art at its natural size, on its own line and centred horizontally within the text area. Drawing first moves down one line, then the image is placed so that it is centred, and the drawing position afterwards sits at the image's bottom-right corner, so following text continues below and to the right of it rather than beside it.

Nothing is drawn if the name given is empty or the single character 0 — a deliberate no-op that is useful when the name is supplied indirectly through a global variable or formula. If the name is not one of the game's images the tag draws nothing and the game logs an error.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. Supplying an empty value or the single character 0 draws nothing instead of failing.

uses.description:
Draws an image whose name is taken from a global variable, rather than written directly into the text. The variable's current contents are read and used as the image name, letting the same piece of text show different pictures as the game state changes. The image is drawn at its natural size on its own line, centred horizontally, with the drawing position afterwards at its bottom-right corner so following text continues below it.

If the variable is empty or holds the single character 0, nothing is drawn — a convenient way to switch the image off entirely. If the variable holds a name that is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the game logs an error.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the global variable to read the image name from. The variable's contents are used as the image name, so the variable must hold the name of one of the game's images, or be empty or 0 to draw nothing.

uses.description:
Draws an image at its natural size only when a condition holds, letting a picture appear or disappear depending on the game state. The condition is a formula that must come out greater than zero; if it does not, or if it is left empty, the tag produces nothing and takes up no space at all.

When the condition passes, drawing moves down one line, the image is centred horizontally within the text area, and the drawing position afterwards sits at its bottom-right corner so following text continues below it. Nothing is drawn if the image name is empty or the single character 0, and an unrecognised image name draws nothing and logs an error.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw when the condition passes, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. Supplying an empty value or the single character 0 draws nothing instead of failing.

required.name: Argument 2
required.description: The condition deciding whether the image appears: it is evaluated against the actor the text belongs to and must come out greater than zero for anything to be drawn. Leaving it empty suppresses the image, and because it is a single argument value it cannot contain an equals sign.

uses.description:
Draws a small image inline with the surrounding text, as a symbol sitting in the flow of a sentence rather than on a line of its own. The image is drawn at its natural size but is treated as three pixels narrower than it really is and is nudged a further three pixels to the left, so it tucks in more tightly against the text on either side than a normal inline icon does.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws a small image inline with the surrounding text, as a symbol sitting in the flow of a sentence rather than on a line of its own. The image is drawn at its natural size but is treated as five pixels narrower than it really is and is nudged a further three pixels to the left, tucking it in more tightly against neighbouring text than either a normal inline icon or the slightly-narrowed variant.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws a small image inline with the surrounding text, as a symbol sitting in the flow of a sentence rather than on a line of its own. The image is drawn at its natural size, shifted three pixels to the left of the current position so it sits snugly after the preceding character, and text resumes immediately to its right.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws a small image inline with the surrounding text, sitting two pixels lower than a normal inline icon and one pixel further left. The lowered placement lines the symbol up better with the baseline of the text around it, which suits icons whose artwork sits high in its frame.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws an image inline with the surrounding text at double size, for a symbol that needs to stand out from the words around it. The image is drawn twice as wide and twice as tall as its artwork, and the drawing position advances by twice the icon's normal width afterwards, so the following text clears the enlarged symbol.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline at double size, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws an image inline with the surrounding text at double size, positioned two pixels lower and one pixel further left than usual so the enlarged symbol lines up better with the baseline of the text around it.

Unlike the plain double-size inline icon, the drawing position afterwards only advances by the icon's normal single width, so the following text overlaps the right-hand half of the enlarged image. This makes the tag suited to a large symbol drawn behind or beneath following text rather than one that needs clear space after it.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline at double size, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws the icon belonging to a particular action inline with the surrounding text, so a piece of text can refer to an ability by showing its symbol rather than naming the image directly. The icon is looked up from the action itself, which means the text automatically follows any change to that action's artwork.

The icon is also drawn using the action's own three palette colours rather than the default text palette, so it appears in the same colours the action uses elsewhere in the interface. It is treated as two pixels wider than its artwork to leave a little breathing room before the following text.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first. If the action's icon is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The ID of the action whose icon should be drawn. The action must exist, otherwise the game fails outright rather than skipping the icon; note that an empty value is silently ignored instead.

uses.description:
Draws the icon belonging to a particular support ability inline with the surrounding text, so a piece of text can refer to a passive ability by showing its symbol rather than naming the image directly. The icon is looked up from the ability itself, which means the text automatically follows any change to that ability's artwork.

The icon is drawn in the default text palette, and is treated as two pixels wider than its artwork to leave a little breathing room before the following text.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first. If the ability's icon is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The ID of the support ability whose icon should be drawn. The ability must exist, otherwise the game fails outright rather than skipping the icon; note that an empty value is silently ignored instead.

uses.description:
Draws an image inline with the surrounding text at half size, for a small unobtrusive symbol. The image is drawn at half its artwork's width and height, shifted four pixels left and four pixels down from where a normal inline icon would sit, and is treated as eight pixels narrower so following text closes up tightly behind it.

If the icon would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line before the icon is placed. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw inline at half size, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

uses.description:
Draws a small image inline with the surrounding text at its natural size, without ever moving to a new line to make room for it. Where the ordinary inline icon jumps to the next line when it would run past the right edge, this one stays put and is drawn where it falls even if that pushes it beyond the width of the text area, which is what you want inside a fixed-width label or a single-line readout that must not reflow.

The image is placed three pixels to the left of the current drawing position, and text resumes immediately to its right. If the name given is empty or is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

optional.name: Argument 1
optional.description: The name of the image to draw inline, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. If omitted the tag draws nothing at all; an empty or unrecognised name is likewise silently ignored.

uses.description:
Places an image behind the text as a backdrop, drawn at double size. The image is added underneath everything else in the text block, so all words and icons appear on top of it, which makes it suited to frames, banners, panels and decorative plates that the text sits within.

The backdrop is centred horizontally across the full width of the containing element, and sits vertically at whatever line the tag appears on, so its vertical placement can be steered by where in the text you write the tag. It does not advance the drawing position, so the text around it continues exactly as if the tag were not there.

Nothing is drawn if the image name is empty or is not one of the game's images; the tag is silently ignored in that case.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw as the backdrop, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: A horizontal offset in pixels added to the centred position, letting you nudge the backdrop left with a negative value or right with a positive one. If omitted the backdrop stays centred. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

optional.name: Argument 3
optional.description: A vertical offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, moving it down with a positive value or up with a negative one. It can only be supplied when a horizontal offset is also given.

uses.description:
Places an image behind the text as a backdrop, drawn at its natural size rather than enlarged. The image is added underneath everything else in the text block, so all words and icons appear on top of it, which makes it suited to frames, banners and decorative plates whose artwork is already drawn at the size it should appear.

The backdrop is positioned as though it were being drawn at double size and centred, so at natural size it sits left of true centre unless nudged with an offset. It sits vertically at whatever line the tag appears on, and does not advance the drawing position, so the text around it continues exactly as if the tag were not there.

Nothing is drawn if the image name is empty or is not one of the game's images; the tag is silently ignored in that case.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw as the backdrop, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: A horizontal offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, letting you nudge it left with a negative value or right with a positive one — commonly needed here to correct for the double-size centring. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

optional.name: Argument 3
optional.description: A vertical offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, moving it down with a positive value or up with a negative one. It can only be supplied when a horizontal offset is also given.

uses.description:
Places an image behind the text as a backdrop, drawn at quadruple size. The image is added underneath everything else in the text block, so all words and icons appear on top of it, which suits large decorative plates and full-panel artwork built from small source images.

The backdrop is positioned as though it were being drawn at double size and centred, so at quadruple size it overhangs both edges evenly around that anchor point. It sits vertically at whatever line the tag appears on, and does not advance the drawing position, so the text around it continues exactly as if the tag were not there.

Nothing is drawn if the image name is empty or is not one of the game's images; the tag is silently ignored in that case.

required.name: Argument 1

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: A horizontal offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, letting you nudge it left with a negative value or right with a positive one. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

optional.name: Argument 3
optional.description: A vertical offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, moving it down with a positive value or up with a negative one. It can only be supplied when a horizontal offset is also given.

uses.description:
Places an image behind the text as a backdrop at double size, but only when a condition holds, so a frame or decorative plate can appear only in the situations that call for it. The condition is a formula that must come out greater than zero; if it does not, or if it is left empty, no backdrop is drawn at all.

When the condition passes the image is added underneath everything else in the text block, centred horizontally across the full width of the containing element and sitting vertically at whatever line the tag appears on. It does not advance the drawing position, so the text around it continues exactly as if the tag were not there.

Unlike the unconditional backdrop tags, this one has no offset arguments — the position after the image name is taken as the condition instead. Nothing is drawn if the image name is empty or is not one of the game's images.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw as the backdrop when the condition passes, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

required.name: Argument 2
required.description: The condition deciding whether the backdrop appears: it is evaluated against the actor the text belongs to and must come out greater than zero for anything to be drawn. Leaving it empty suppresses the backdrop, and because it is a single argument value it cannot contain an equals sign.

uses.description:
Places an image behind the text as a backdrop at double size, aligned hard against the left edge of the text area rather than centred. This is the variant to use for a backdrop whose artwork is already sized to the full panel, or one that should butt up against the left margin regardless of how wide the containing element happens to be.

The image is added underneath everything else in the text block, so all words and icons appear on top of it, and it sits vertically at whatever line the tag appears on. It does not advance the drawing position, so the text around it continues exactly as if the tag were not there.

Nothing is drawn if the image name is empty or is not one of the game's images; the tag is silently ignored in that case.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the image to draw as the backdrop, which must be one of the images in the game's art set. An empty or unrecognised name silently draws nothing.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: A horizontal offset in pixels from the left edge, letting you inset the backdrop with a positive value or push it off the left edge with a negative one. If omitted the backdrop starts exactly at the left edge. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

optional.name: Argument 3
optional.description: A vertical offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, moving it down with a positive value or up with a negative one. It can only be supplied when a horizontal offset is also given.

uses.description:
Places an image behind the text as a backdrop at double size, taking the image's name from a global variable rather than writing it directly into the text. This lets the same piece of text show a different frame or plate as the game state changes — for example a backdrop that reflects the player's current faction or ship.

The backdrop is centred horizontally across the full width of the containing element and sits vertically at whatever line the tag appears on. It is added underneath everything else in the text block, so all words and icons appear on top of it, and it does not advance the drawing position.

If the variable holds the single character 0, or is empty, or holds a name that is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn — giving a convenient way to switch the backdrop off entirely.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the global variable to read the backdrop's image name from. The variable's contents are used as the image name, so the variable must hold the name of one of the game's images, or hold 0 or nothing to draw no backdrop. The variable name itself must not be empty.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: A horizontal offset in pixels added to the centred position, letting you nudge the backdrop left with a negative value or right with a positive one. If omitted the backdrop stays centred. A value that is not a valid decimal number causes an error rather than being ignored.

optional.name: Argument 3
optional.description: A vertical offset in pixels added to the backdrop's position, moving it down with a positive value or up with a negative one. It can only be supplied when a horizontal offset is also given.

This combines a state-driven backdrop with left-edge alignment, for panel artwork that should fill from the margin regardless of how wide the containing element is.

The image is added underneath everything else in the text block, so all words and icons appear on top of it, and it sits vertically at whatever line the tag appears on. It does not advance the drawing position, so the text around it continues exactly as if the tag were not there.

If the variable holds the single character 0, or is empty, or holds a name that is not one of the game's images, nothing is drawn — giving a convenient way to switch the backdrop off entirely.

uses.description:
Draws a damage readout inline with the text: a coloured elemental badge with a number sitting on top of it, in the compact numeral font the game uses for damage figures. This is the presentation used in ability and item descriptions to show how much damage of a given element something deals.

The number is taken literally from the text rather than being calculated, which is what distinguishes this tag from the calculating variants — use it when the figure is already known, is a range such as 3-5, or is anything else a formula could not produce. The badge is placed slightly above the text baseline and the number is nudged left as it gets longer so that it stays visually centred on the badge.

The badge never wraps to a new line, so it is drawn where it falls even if that runs past the right edge. The whole tag is silently skipped if fewer than two values are supplied.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The element whose badge artwork is drawn behind the number, which determines the colour and symbol of the readout. Only elements that have badge artwork in the game can be used; naming one that does not causes the game to fail outright rather than skipping the badge.

required.name: Argument 2
required.description: The text drawn on top of the badge, used exactly as written with no calculation applied. Longer values are shifted further left to stay centred on the badge, and because this is a single argument value it cannot contain an equals sign.

uses.description:
Draws a damage readout inline with the text: a coloured elemental badge with a calculated number sitting on top of it, in the compact numeral font the game uses for damage figures, with a leading plus sign when the result is positive. The explicit sign makes it suited to modifiers and bonuses, where the reader needs to see at a glance whether a figure adds or subtracts.

The number is worked out by evaluating a formula against the actor the text belongs to and rounding the result up to a whole number, so the badge shows the value as it applies to that particular character rather than a fixed figure. Negative results keep their own minus sign and are shown unchanged; zero is shown without a sign.

The badge is placed slightly above the text baseline and the number is nudged left as it gets longer so that it stays visually centred on the badge. It never wraps to a new line, so it is drawn where it falls even if that runs past the right edge. The whole tag is silently skipped if fewer than two values are supplied.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The element whose badge artwork is drawn behind the number, which determines the colour and symbol of the readout. Only elements that have badge artwork in the game can be used; naming one that does not causes the game to fail outright rather than skipping the badge.

required.name: Argument 2
required.description: The formula giving the number shown on the badge. It is evaluated against the actor the text belongs to and rounded up to a whole number, and because it is a single argument value it cannot contain an equals sign.

uses.description:
Draws an item's sprite inline with the surrounding text at normal tile size, taking the item's ID from a global variable rather than writing it directly into the text. This lets a single piece of text show whichever item the game state currently points at — the player's equipped weapon, a quest reward chosen at runtime, and so on.

The sprite is drawn in the item's own palette colours, so it looks exactly as it does in the inventory. If the sprite would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first. If the variable holds an ID that is not a known item, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the item ID to draw. The variable's contents are looked up as an item, so it must hold the ID of an existing item type or nothing is drawn.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: How many of the item the sprite should represent. Items whose artwork changes with stack size show a fuller pile at higher numbers; for every other item this makes no visible difference. Defaults to one, and a value that is not a whole number causes an error rather than being ignored.

uses.description:
Draws an item's sprite inline with the surrounding text at normal tile size, sitting three pixels lower than usual so it lines up better with the baseline of the text around it, and taking the item's ID from a global variable rather than writing it directly into the text. This lets a single piece of text show whichever item the game state currently points at.

The sprite is drawn in the item's own palette colours, so it looks exactly as it does in the inventory. If the sprite would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first. If the variable holds an ID that is not a known item, nothing is drawn and the tag is silently ignored.

required.name: Argument 1
required.description: The name of the global variable holding the item ID to draw. The variable's contents are looked up as an item, so it must hold the ID of an existing item type or nothing is drawn.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: How many of the item the sprite should represent. Items whose artwork changes with stack size show a fuller pile at higher numbers; for every other item this makes no visible difference. Defaults to one, and a value that is not a whole number causes an error rather than being ignored.

This lets a line of dialog or a description refer to whatever item the game state currently points at — the weapon the player is holding, a randomly chosen reward, the goods a trader is after — and have the right name appear.

Draws a character type's standard sprite inline with the surrounding text, at the size that character normally appears in the world. The sprite is drawn in the character type's own armour, skin and clothing palettes, so it looks like a typical member of that kind rather than any particular individual in the game.

The sprite is pulled up and to the left by a quarter of its size, so it overlaps the line above and hangs slightly into the preceding text — the placement that makes a character read as standing in the sentence rather than sitting on the baseline. Text resumes to its right.

If the sprite would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first. Nothing is drawn if the character type does not exist or has no standard sprite defined; naming a character that exists in the world rather than a character type also draws nothing.

optional.name: Argument 2
optional.description: Which facing direction to draw, given as a row number in the character's sprite sheet counting from zero. Character types that do not have separate rows per facing ignore this entirely, and a value that is not a whole number causes an error rather than being ignored.

uses.description:
Draws a particular character's head inline with the surrounding text, so a line of dialog or a report can show who is being talked about. Unlike the character-type sprite tags, this draws a specific individual who exists in the world, using that individual's own armour, skin and clothing colours, so the picture reflects how they actually look right now.

The head sprite is drawn first and the character's face is drawn on top of it, giving the complete portrait. The picture is aligned to the current text position rather than being pulled up and left, so it sits in line with the words around it, and text resumes to its right.

A character who has died is still drawn, but in the game's washed-out colours for the dead rather than their own. Nothing is drawn if the name given matches neither a character in the world nor a fallen party member, or if that character has no head sprite. If the picture would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first.

optional.description: Which facing direction to draw, given as a row number in the ship's sprite sheet counting from zero. Ship types that do not have separate rows per facing ignore this entirely, and a value that is not a whole number causes an error rather than being ignored.

uses.description:
Draws the sprite of one of the ships in the player's own fleet, inline with the surrounding text at its normal world size, sitting six pixels lower than usual so it lines up better with the baseline of the text around it. The ship is picked by its position in the fleet, so a piece of text can show the player's flagship, or their second or third vessel, without knowing in advance what type of ship that is.

The sprite is drawn in that ship type's own palettes and is pulled up and to the left by a quarter of its size before the drop is applied; text resumes to its right at the original height. If it would not fit in the space left on the current line, drawing wraps to the start of the next line first.

Nothing is drawn if the fleet has no ship at the requested position, or if the ship type has no standard sprite defined.
